claims.subject: Candidate Processor
claims.evidence_quote: Each processor x maintains a counter T (x), referred to as a token counter, which tracks the number of triggers received by x.

claims.subject: Token
claims.evidence_quote: A single token is defined as the receipt of τ triggers, i.e., a token is accumulated every time the count reaches a multiple of τ.

claims.subject: Threshold Value
claims.evidence_quote: Each processor computes a threshold value τ = ⌊ w2n⌋, where w is the total number of triggers required to raise the alert.

claims.subject: Candidate Processor
claims.evidence_quote: All the candidate processors form a committee.

claims.subject: Rank
claims.evidence_quote: The rank becomes the ID of the processor.

claims.subject: Chernoff Bound
claims.evidence_quote: The range is chosen such that all n ranks are distinct with high probability, which follows from a standard Chernoff bound analysis [13].

claims.subject: Phase 1
claims.evidence_quote: In that case, each processor calculates the threshold value (τ = ⌊w1∕2n⌋) where w1 is the number of triggers left to count after which the alert should be raised.

claims.subject: Candidate Processor
claims.evidence_quote: At last, the non-faulty processors raise the alert (see Lemma 2).

claims.subject: Candidate Processor
claims.evidence_quote: Whenever a candidate processor gets to know about any trigger token, that candidate processor broadcasts the message to all other candidate processors.
